major.fix: Change Second Main Event step 2 to: "Add a fifth: she trickles rice from a height into the bowl, over a tray, with Kreston in the high chair or out of the room. Record that one twice, high and low, then tip the rice back into the lidded tub and sweep the floor before he is down."

major.problem: The 4:15 row puts the day's sharp tools on the floor and the Safety block covers only the grater in use. Main Event materials: "1 box grater (adult holds it)," "1 garlic press, or the flat of a knife." Infant Integration: "Say the tool names out loud as Azlyn tests them and he takes two into his mouth and one into his vocabulary." Schedule 4:15-5:00: "Quiet Play: The Tool Drawer on the Floor." Safety block: "A box grater takes knuckles off, so you hold it and she pushes the cheese. The soup pan goes on the back burner with the handle turned in." Nothing anywhere covers a whole tool drawer at floor level with a 17-month-old who is on record mouthing the tools.
major.fix: Add to the Safety block, before the pan sentence: "Take the grater, the peeler, the can opener and anything with a point out of the tray before it goes down on the floor, and leave her the spoons, the masher, the whisk and the measuring cups. Kreston mouths every tool he reaches at 17 months, so he works this one beside you or not at all."

major.problem: A step destroys the result the Tip and the week opener state. Main Event step 3: "let her pick three spots: open ground, under something, tight against a wall." Step 5: "If the sky stays dry, hand her the watering can and let her rain on all three from the same height, counting to five over each." Tip: "The bottle under the porch catches nothing. Read it out anyway and let her tell you why." Week 46 opener: "Friday she stands three bottles in three places and finds that where a thing sits changes how much rain lands in it." Watering each bottle directly fills the sheltered one to the same line as the others, so the sheltered bottle catches everything and the day's finding is gone.
major.fix: Change Main Event step 5 to: "If the sky stays dry, hand her the watering can and rain from one spot only, standing in the open and holding the can high, so the water falls where it would fall. Count to five and let her walk round and read all three. The one under cover stays dry, and that is the answer."

major.problem: The 4:15 row undoes an explicit instruction from the afternoon and reaches for a chart already put up. Second Main Event step 5: "Write TOMORROW across the eighth square and leave it empty." Step 6: "Let her draw her guess in the corner, small." Step 7: "Stick it on the fridge at her height with the magnet, and check her guess against the window at breakfast." Schedule 4:15-5:00: "Quiet Play: Drawing on the Blank Squares." There is one blank square, it is under an instruction to stay empty until breakfast, and it is on the fridge by 2:30.
major.fix: Change the 4:15 schedule row to: "4:15-5:00 PM - Quiet Play: The Leftover Symbol Cards" and change the Quiet Play reference so she draws more weather symbols on the spare cards instead of on the chart.

major.problem: The day hangs loose string at toddler height outdoors and ties ribbon within a strapped-in baby's reach, and the Safety block never mentions either. Main Event materials: "String, 3 feet." Step 4: "Tape one end of the string to the ring." Step 5: "Tie it to the fence at her eye height, in sight of the kitchen window." Step 6: "Check it again at lunch and before dinner." Kreston's Afternoon: "Tie a ribbon to his stroller handle and let him watch it go while you walk." Safety block covers fasteners, offcut bag strips, the whole bag and the scissors, and stops there. A three-foot string on a fence at a three-year-old's eye height is at a 17-month-old's reach, and it stays out all day.
major.fix: Add to the Safety block: "Tie the windsock string short, so no loop hangs below the ring, and hang it above Kreston's reach rather than at hers if she can still see the tails from the kitchen window. The stroller ribbon goes on the outside of the handle where he cannot get it round anything, and comes off the moment the walk ends."

major.problem: Prep Tonight empties the room the night before, then the 8:00 block makes emptying it the activity. Prep Tonight: "Clear the floor in front of the sofa, leave a blanket and two cushions on it and everything else out of the room, and put the library bag by the door." Opening Activity step 1: "Anything that is not the blanket, the cushions or the three villagers goes out of the room. She carries most of it, and the carrying is half the activity." Nothing is left for her to carry.
major.fix: Change Prep Tonight to: "Stand a blanket and two cushions by the sofa and put the library bag by the door. Leave the room exactly as it is, because clearing it is her first job in the morning."

major.problem: The 8:00 block puts a plastic bag and a pile of candy wrappers on the floor with a walking 18-month-old in the room, and no line anywhere covers it. Opening Activity: "Spread the lot on the floor by the window and let her hold each piece up to the light" (materials: wax paper, candy wrappers, 1 clear plastic folder, 1 freezer bag). Infant Integration keeps Kreston in the room: "give him one of his own and let him point it at the ceiling. Keep him at the table end while the cutting happens." The Safety block covers only tea-light batteries, the craft knife and the scissors.
major.fix: Add to the Safety block: "The freezer bag and the plastic folder come up off the floor the moment the sorting ends, because a bag at floor level suffocates an 18-month-old, and the candy wrappers get counted out and counted back into the box."

major.problem: The 4:00 row clears the flour the 4:15 row needs. Schedule: "4:00-4:15 PM - Her Job: Wiping the Flour Off the Table" then "4:15-5:00 PM - Quiet Play: Drawing in the Flour." The table she draws on was wiped clean fifteen minutes earlier.
major.fix: Change the 4:15 row to: "**4:15–5:00 PM** — Quiet Play: Drawing in Flour on the Baking Tray" (the day already carries a baking tray in the Main Event materials list).

major.problem: Loose screws go in at a three-year-old's height while a 17-month-old with a pincer grip works the next cupboard door, and the Safety block names the screwdriver but never the screws. Main Event step 4: "Stick or screw the hook on the end of the unit at her height." Infant Integration: "give him the second cloth and a low cupboard door to wipe while Azlyn does her drawer." Safety: "The screwdriver goes back in your pocket between turns on the hook."
major.fix: Extend that Safety sentence to: "The screws and the screwdriver both go back in your pocket between turns on the hook, and the floor gets checked before Kreston is loose in the room, because a screw is pincer-grip size at 17 months. Use the adhesive pads if he is in the kitchen with you."

major.problem: The walk brings choke-sized foraging home and parks it at an 18-month-old's height, with no line covering it. Get Outside: "Walk the block hunting for what is still standing in December: rose hips, pine cones, the dry heads of goldenrod and Queen Anne's lace, acorn caps... Bring back one thing for each page she filled and lay them on the shelf beside the book." Prep Tonight: "clear a low shelf for the book to live on." The Safety block covers the bedsheet and the twenty bottle caps and stops there. Day 333's own Safety block already treats fir cones and seed cases as choke-sized for Kreston.
major.fix: Change the last Get Outside sentence to: "Bring back one thing for each page she filled and stand them in a bowl on a high shelf above the book, because rose hips and acorn caps are choke-sized for an 18-month-old and the book shelf is one he can reach."

major.problem: The page gives four different answers about when flour leaves the floor. Infant Integration: "Put his hand flat in the flour and lift it straight up... He does it with two hands as long as the floor stays floured." Safety: "sweep the flour up before Kreston is put down, because a floured floor is slick under new walkers." Second Main Event opener: "The flour trail wipes off the floor at four" (the 4:00 row is Her Job: Wiping the Table). Main Event step 6: "Let her lay a fresh trail across the hall for Joseph to find tonight," which puts a second floured floor down for the whole evening with a walking 18-month-old on it. A reader following the Safety block cannot run the infant block or step 6.
major.fix: Replace the Safety sentence with: "Keep the flour to the one stretch of kitchen floor you can see across, stay beside Kreston every second he is printing on it, and sweep it up the moment the story is told, because a floured floor is slick under new walkers." Then change step 6 to: "Let her lay a fresh trail across the hall after Kreston is in bed, for Joseph to find tonight," and change the Second Main Event opener to "The flour trail comes off the floor before lunch."

major.problem: The scene the day builds puts choking-size objects on the kitchen floor and then puts Kreston on that floor, with no line anywhere covering them. Prep Tonight: "a scatter of seed, the cup on its side, a tuft of cotton by the door." Materials: "A handful of sunflower seeds" and "1 cotton ball pulled into a tuft of fur." Infant Integration: "he follows Azlyn along the trail doing his version of whatever she does." The Safety block covers only salt dough, the oven and slippery flour. Seeds and a pulled cotton tuft are exactly what an 18-month-old picks up with a pincer grip and mouths.
major.fix: Add to the Safety block: "The sunflower seeds and the cotton tuft go off the floor and into your pocket the moment their sticky notes are read, because both are choking size at 18 months and he is down there on the trail with her."

major.problem: The afternoon moves the houseplants to floor level and hands one to Kreston, and nothing on the page covers leaves or soil. Step 4: "Two big squares of masking tape on the floor, and everything she can carry goes in the right one, houseplants included." Kreston's Afternoon: "Let him carry one houseplant to its square with both arms." The Safety block is packaging only: "Button batteries out of new toys go up and out of the house, wire ties and plastic film go straight into the trash bag, ribbon does not stay on the floor." Common houseplants (pothos, philodendron, peace lily, dieffenbachia) burn a mouth, and the soil goes in first.
major.fix: Add to the Safety block: "Houseplant leaves and potting soil go straight in his mouth at 18 months, so you carry the pots and he walks beside you, keep the taped squares where he is not free to graze, and every plant goes back up on its shelf before the photograph."

major.problem: The page both clears the foil coins and leaves them out. Step 7: "Everything into the basket, counted against her map. Two coins go back out at her height so she gets a turn at finding," and the schedule keeps them out through "4:15-5:00 Quiet Play: The Coins She Kept Back." Against that, Safety: "The foil-wrapped coins are a choking hazard at 18 months, so count them out and count them back into the basket," and Kreston's Afternoon: "The foil coins are not for him, so run his round first and sweep before he is down." Azlyn's height at four is climbing height for a boy who has climbed since sixteen months, and the quiet-play hour is his floor time.
major.fix: Change step 7 to: "Everything into the basket, counted against her map. Two coins go back out for her own turn while Kreston is in the high chair, and both are counted back into the basket before he is down again."

major.problem: Get Outside and the Safety block give opposite instructions for the same four objects. Get Outside: "She is four, so she collects four things and carries them home in her hands... acorn caps, a sweetgum ball, a pine cone, a bare twig." Infant Integration: "Acorn caps and the sweetgum ball stay with Azlyn." Safety: "Acorn caps and the sweetgum ball are all choking size at 18 months, so they travel in your pocket." A reader following the walk block hands a climbing, mouthing 18-month-old a fistful of acorn caps at his eye level.
major.fix: Change the Get Outside sentence to: "She is four, so she picks four things and hands each one straight up to your pocket, then counts all four back out on the doorstep," and change the infant line to "Acorn caps and the sweetgum ball ride in your pocket."

major.problem: Prep Tonight: "Dig out the twelve handprint sheets and stand them on the table with the scissors." Safety on the same page: "The scissors open three sealed things today, so they go back up out of reach between each one and never onto the table." The page leaves the scissors on the table overnight, and 8:00 opens with both children at that table (Kreston 18 months, climbing since sixteen).
major.fix: Prep Tonight becomes: "Dig out the twelve handprint sheets and stand them on the table. The scissors stay up out of reach; they come down in your hand three times tomorrow and go straight back."

major.problem: Get Outside: "Walk the block counting lit windows, then count again at 5:00 to see how different the same houses look." The schedule gives 5:00-5:45 PM to "🛁 Wind-Down: Mom Reads, Nobody Moves", and 4:15-5:00 to Quiet Play. The second count has no hour to happen in, and it walks the family out of the wind-down on the one day built around the adult sitting down.
major.fix: Get Outside sentence becomes: "Walk the block counting lit windows, then count the same houses again from the front window at 5:45, with the light gone and dinner nearly on."

major.problem: Bad Weather Day 2 Safety: 'Keep all four saucers on a high shelf: Kreston will eat what is on them.' Step 5: 'Line all four up beside her morning drawing at four o'clock,' and the schedule gives '4:15–5:00 PM — Quiet Play: The Four Saucers Again' — forty-five minutes of a 16-month-old loose in the room with four saucers of cut apple, one of them soaked in lemon or vinegar, down at her level.
major.fix: Change the schedule row to '4:15–5:00 PM — Quiet Play: The Four Saucers, Looked At From Your Arms' and add to step 5: 'Hold each saucer for her, one at a time, and put it straight back on the high shelf. Nothing on those saucers comes down to floor level while Kreston is in the room.'

major.problem: Bad Weather Day 2 Safety: 'every bowl gets emptied the moment you leave the room, with no exceptions for a quick errand,' echoed in Kreston's Afternoon: 'Empty every bowl of water the moment you step away from it.' The schedule then reads '4:00–4:15 PM — Her Job: Emptying the Rinse Bowl' — a bowl last used at 10:15 that morning, still standing full of water six hours later with a 9-month-old who pulls up on everything.
major.fix: Change the row to '4:00–4:15 PM — Her Job: The Clean End Put Away' and change the job to drying and shelving the washed things, since the rinse bowl went down the sink at 10:15.

major.problem: Bad Weather Day 2, Instead of Getting Outside: 'keep a tally with two piles of buttons on the sill,' for forty-five minutes at the window. The same page holds Kreston up at that window to point and name, and its Safety block covers pot handles, the gate, the sharp knife and raw vegetable pieces, saying nothing about the buttons. The book's own January page states a button is the right size to block an airway, and he is 15 months and fast here.
major.fix: Change the line to 'keep a tally with two piles of clothespins on the sill' and add to the Safety block: 'Nothing smaller than his fist goes on the sill while he is up at the glass with you.'

major.problem: September Extra Ideas carries no Safety block, only the shared line about water, small parts and taped doorways. Two of its entries run on buckeyes: 'Six Bottles Down the Hallway, bowling with the fattest buckeye in the bowl' and 'Buckeye Faces, a marker, a bowl of buckeyes, and a family of them along the sill.' A buckeye is a choking size for a running 15-month-old and it is poisonous chewed, which the 'small parts up off the floor' line does not reach. Of the twelve extras pages this is the one that needs a Safety block of its own.
major.fix: Add above the activity list: '⚠️ Safety: Buckeyes are poisonous chewed and they are exactly the size Kreston chokes on, so they stay on the table or on the sill, get counted out and counted back into the bowl, and the bowl goes up high the moment she is finished. Wash both sets of hands after. Same rule for the coins in the change jar and the dry seed heads.'

major.problem: Bad Weather Day 2, Second Main Event step 5: 'Stand the mirror against the wall,' materials calling for '1 mirror, or the biggest one you can carry into the room,' and step 7 leaving it there: 'the basket stays in that room with the mirror for four o'clock,' with 4:15–5:00 given to 'Quiet Play: The Clothes Pile and the Mirror.' Kreston's Afternoon on the same page says 'At 13 months he climbs anything with a lip on it.' The Safety block covers heat, parked cars, frozen bottles and the floor fan, and says nothing about a large mirror leaning free against a wall for four hours.
major.fix: Change step 5 to: 'Stand the mirror flat against the wall behind the sofa or hang it, and put a hand on it to check it cannot walk out at the base. A leaning mirror comes down on a 13-month-old who pulls on it, so if it will not sit solid, take everybody to the bathroom mirror instead.'
